questions.question: A conservative force is one for which the work done between two points:
options: Is independent of the path taken
Depends on the speed of the object

questions.question: Which force below is NON-conservative?
options: The force between two magnets held at rest
The weight of a falling stone

questions.question: Mechanical energy is defined as:
options: The sum of kinetic and gravitational potential energy

questions.question: A stone is dropped from 4,9 m with air resistance ignored. Using conservation of mechanical energy, it lands at:

subtopics.title: The Equation W n c Equals Delta E k Plus Delta E p

questions.question: The equation Wnc = ΔEk + ΔEp states that the work done by non-conservative forces equals:
options: The change in kinetic energy plus the change in potential energy
The heat produced by the engine

questions.question: A 40 kg child slides from rest down a 2,5 m high slide, arriving at 5 m·s⁻¹. ΔEp for the ride is:
For that ride, ΔEk = +500 J and ΔEp = −980 J, so the work done by friction is:
A NEGATIVE value of Wnc tells you that:
options: Energy was drained from the system, usually by friction
Energy was pumped into the system by a motor

subtopics.title: Working the Equation on Slopes and Rough Ground

questions.question: A 3 kg box slides from rest down a rough 5 m ramp whose top is 2 m high, arriving at 4 m·s⁻¹. Wnc is:
To convert friction's work of −34,8 J into a force, you divide by:
options: The 2 m height of the ramp
The 5 m length of the ramp surface

questions.question: A winch hauls the box back up the ramp at constant speed. The winch's work must equal:
options: Only the gain in potential energy
The gain in potential energy plus the friction losses
Zero, because the speed is constant

questions.question: A ball thrown upward returns to the hand slower than it left because air resistance:
options: Does negative work on the way up and positive work on the way down
Acts only on the way up
Does negative work on both the way up and the way down

subtopics.title: Power — the Rate of Doing Work

questions.question: Power is defined as:
options: The rate at which work is done
The total energy of a system

questions.question: A 55 kg learner runs up stairs 3,2 m high in 4 s. The learner's power output against gravity is:
A pump raises 150 kg of water per minute from a 25 m deep borehole at steady speed. Its minimum power is:
A bus holds a constant 20 m·s⁻¹ against total resistive forces of 2 500 N. The power delivered is:
In the banker-and-toll-collector picture, gravity is the honest banker because:
options: It charges for height and repays in full on the way down, whatever the route
It charges per metre of path travelled
It only acts on heavy objects

questions.question: Friction is the toll collector because it:
options: Repays its charges when you return
Charges per metre of path and never refunds, turning the payment into heat
Only charges on the way down

questions.question: A girl on a swing rises slightly less on each pass because:
options: Her potential energy is converting to kinetic energy
Gravity takes energy without repaying it
Non-conservative forces are draining her mechanical energy as heat
Her mass decreases with each swing

questions.question: The child entered the slide with 980 J of potential energy and arrived with 500 J of kinetic energy. Friction's receipt reads:
A POSITIVE Wnc on the receipt means:
options: Energy was paid into the system by an engine or a person

questions.question: A frictionless slide would deliver the child at 7 m·s⁻¹; she actually arrives at 5 m·s⁻¹. This alone proves:
options: The slide is steeper than expected
Her mass changed on the way down
Energy left the system through non-conservative forces

questions.question: When converting friction's work to a force on a ramp, and potential energy to joules, you must use respectively:
options: The height for friction and the path length for gravity
The path length for friction and the vertical height for gravity

questions.question: Two learners carry identical boxes up the same stairs, one in 4 s and one in 40 s. Compared with the slow learner, the fast one does:
options: The same work at ten times the power
Ten times the work at the same power

questions.question: One watt equals:
For a vehicle cruising at constant speed v against a resisting force F, the power delivered is:
The pump's 'minimum power' refers to:
options: The smallest motor the shop sells
Gravity's bill alone, paid on schedule — real pumps must also cover pipe friction
The power when the pump runs empty
Half the rated power of the motor
